sentences.text: The genus Scapanorhynchus includes four known species: S. lewisii, S. texanus, S. rapax, and S. raphiodon.
While Scapanorhynchus usually did not exceed 4.15 meters in length, the largest teeth found suggest some individuals could reach up to 6.7 meters.
The genus Scapanorhynchus was first described by Woodward in 1889.
Scapanorhynchus was likely a pelagic apex predator living in the epipelagic zone or on the continental shelf.
Isotopic analysis of its teeth indicates that Scapanorhynchus primarily ate fish and occupied a high trophic level.
Scapanorhynchus fed on crustaceans, clams, and small fish.
Scapanorhynchus lived during the Cretaceous period, from the Aptian stage to the end of the Maastrichtian stage.
Fossil records place Scapanorhynchus in existence from the Barremian to the Serravallian, between 125.77 and 11.63 million years ago.
A potentially new youngest record of Scapanorhynchus cf. raphiodon was found in Upper Cretaceous (Campanian) strata of the Duwi Formation in Egypt.
Some experts suggest reclassifying Scapanorhynchus as Scapanorhynchus owstoni due to its extreme similarity to the living goblin shark, though most specialists disagree.
Records of Scapanorhynchus from the Miocene, such as S. subulatus, are considered dubious and may actually be misidentified sand sharks.
